test.title: Mini-test · Learning a language as an adult

paragraphs.text: It is widely believed that adults cannot learn a foreign language as well as children. Like many popular beliefs, this one contains some truth and a great deal of exaggeration. Research does suggest that people who begin learning in early childhood are more likely to develop a native-like accent. But accent is only one part of language, and in my view it is the part that matters least.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Adults, in fact, have several advantages. They can understand grammatical explanations, use dictionaries efficiently and apply strategies they have developed in other areas of learning. In the early stages, adult beginners often make faster progress than children, who need far more hours of exposure before they can use a new language with confidence.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Why, then, do so many adults give up? I suspect the main reason is not age but time. A child at an international school may hear a language for six hours a day; an adult attending an evening class may manage three hours a week. It is hardly surprising that the results differ. Embarrassment also plays a part. Adults are used to being competent, and many find it uncomfortable to sound clumsy in front of others.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Technology has made self-study easier than ever, and language apps now have millions of users. They are useful for building vocabulary, but I am sceptical of claims that an app alone can make someone fluent. Speaking a language is a social skill, and it develops through conversation with real people.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: My advice to adult learners is therefore simple. Accept that you may never sound like a native speaker, and do not treat this as failure. Aim to be understood rather than to be perfect, find people to talk to as early as possible, and measure your progress in months rather than weeks.
paragraphs.label: E

document.title: Mini-test · Learning a language as an adult

items.quote: this one contains some truth and a great deal of exaggeration
items.prompt: The writer believes the idea that adults cannot learn languages well is completely false.

explanation.en: “contains some truth and a great deal of exaggeration” — the writer says the belief is partly true. “Completely false” contradicts this → NO.
explanation.kk: «contains some truth and a great deal of exaggeration» — автордың айтуынша, бұл пікірде шындықтың үлесі бар. «Completely false» бұған қайшы → NO.
explanation.ru: «contains some truth and a great deal of exaggeration» — в этом мнении, по словам автора, есть доля правды. «Completely false» противоречит → NO.

items.quote: in my view it is the part that matters least
items.prompt: The writer thinks accent is the least important part of language.

explanation.en: On accent the writer says directly: “in my view it is the part that matters least”. The part that matters least is the least important → YES.
explanation.kk: Акцент туралы автор тікелей айтады: «in my view it is the part that matters least». «Matters least» дегені — ең маңызсыз бөлік → YES.
explanation.ru: Об акценте автор говорит прямо: «in my view it is the part that matters least». Часть, которая «matters least», — наименее важная → YES.

items.quote: In the early stages, adult beginners often make faster progress than children
items.prompt: The writer claims that adult beginners can make quicker early progress than children.

explanation.en: “In the early stages, adult beginners often make faster progress than children” — “quicker early progress” paraphrases this → YES.
explanation.kk: «In the early stages, adult beginners often make faster progress than children» — «quicker early progress» осының басқаша айтылымы → YES.
explanation.ru: «In the early stages, adult beginners often make faster progress than children» — «quicker early progress» пересказывает это → YES.

items.prompt: The writer believes most language teachers use outdated methods.

explanation.en: Nothing is said about teachers’ methods: the text is about adult learners’ abilities. The writer’s view is unknown → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Мұғалімдердің әдістері туралы мәтінде ештеңе жоқ: ересек оқушылардың қабілеті туралы айтылады. Автордың пікірі белгісіз → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: О методах преподавателей в тексте ничего нет: речь о способностях взрослых учеников. Мнение автора неизвестно → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: I suspect the main reason is not age but time
items.prompt: According to the writer, lack of time matters more than age when adults give up.

explanation.en: “I suspect the main reason is not age but time” — for the writer the main reason is time, not age → YES. “I suspect” is cautious, but it is still his view.
explanation.kk: «I suspect the main reason is not age but time» — автордың ойынша, басты себеп жас емес, уақыт → YES. «I suspect» сақ айтылған, бірақ бұл — автордың ұстанымы.
explanation.ru: «I suspect the main reason is not age but time» — главная причина, по мнению автора, время, а не возраст → YES. «I suspect» — осторожно, но это позиция автора.

items.quote: many find it uncomfortable to sound clumsy in front of others
items.prompt: The writer believes adults generally feel comfortable making mistakes in front of others.

explanation.en: “many find it uncomfortable to sound clumsy in front of others” — adults find it awkward, not comfortable → NO.
explanation.kk: «many find it uncomfortable to sound clumsy in front of others» — ересектерге басқалардың алдында қателесу ыңғайсыз → NO.
explanation.ru: «many find it uncomfortable to sound clumsy in front of others» — взрослым как раз неловко ошибаться при других → NO.

items.quote: They are useful for building vocabulary
items.prompt: The writer thinks language apps are of no use to learners.

explanation.en: The writer is sceptical only that an app can make someone fluent; he says “They are useful for building vocabulary” → NO.
explanation.kk: Автор қосымша адамды еркін сөйлетеді дегенге ғана күмәнмен қарайды, бірақ «They are useful for building vocabulary» дейді → NO.
explanation.ru: Автор скептичен только к тому, что приложение сделает человека свободно говорящим, но пишет «They are useful for building vocabulary» → NO.

items.quote: language apps now have millions of users
items.prompt: The writer considers language apps more expensive than evening classes.

explanation.en: The text never compares the cost of apps and evening classes. Evening classes are mentioned only in relation to time → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Қосымша мен кешкі курстың бағасы мәтінде салыстырылмайды. Кешкі курс тек уақытқа байланысты аталады → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Цены приложений и вечерних курсов в тексте не сравниваются. Вечерние курсы упомянуты только в связи со временем → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: find people to talk to as early as possible
items.prompt: The writer recommends that adults start talking to people early in their learning.

explanation.en: The writer’s advice: “find people to talk to as early as possible” → YES.
explanation.kk: Автордың ұсынысы: «find people to talk to as early as possible» → YES.
explanation.ru: Совет автора: «find people to talk to as early as possible» → YES.

items.quote: measure your progress in months rather than weeks
items.prompt: The writer thinks adult learners should expect clear progress within a few weeks.

explanation.en: “measure your progress in months rather than weeks” — progress should be judged over months, not weeks → NO.
explanation.kk: «measure your progress in months rather than weeks» — прогресті апталармен емес, айлармен бағалау керек → NO.
explanation.ru: «measure your progress in months rather than weeks» — прогресс стоит оценивать месяцами, а не неделями → NO.

groups.instruction: Questions 1–10. Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in the reading passage? Write YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer, NO if the statement contradicts the claims of the writer, or NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
